answer: Random beacon draws: which agents sit on which jury is decided by unpredictable randomness each epoch, never by choice or schedule. A colluding ring cannot predict or arrange its co-assignments, so to steer outcomes it must bribe a random sample of an ocean of jurors per round - and each caught juror faces slashing plus ejection, while the honest grove simply keeps serving. Expected gain collapses below expected cost: subverting one fixed committee is cheap, subverting a fresh random draw every six hours is not. The mechanism costs nothing to honest participants; it prices attacks in luck.
